#  11818 - Student Workshop School Meets Science Modulübersicht  
|  Module Number:   | **11818**  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Module Title:  | **Student Workshop School Meets Science**  |  
|  Studentenworkshop Schule trifft Wissenschaft   |  
| Department:  |  Faculty 2 - Environment and Natural Sciences   |  
| Responsible Staff Member:  | 
  * Dr. rer. nat. Hansen, Barbara 

 |  
| Language of Teaching / Examination:  | English  |  
| Duration:  | 1 semester  |  
| Frequency of Offer:  |  Every winter semester   |  
| Credits:  |  
| Learning Outcome:  | 
  * BTU students will learn how to organise a workshop for high-school students on the subject of biotechnology in an independent team. In general they will learn to arrange non-specialist lectures and demonstrations, organising scientific events for younger people and other cross-disciplinary participants, and to improve their public appearance.
  * After completing the workshop, BTU students will be able to communicate expert knowledge to high-school students in short lectures. BTU students will especially have learnt to adjust to the level of knowledge of a particular audience like high-school students.

 |  
| Contents:  | 
  * In order to increase the interest of prospective students in the university, high-school students of grades 10–13 could take part in a workshop on the subject of biotechnology and adjacent topics at BTU. The workshop includes short presentations of BTU students and scientists on current biotechnology topics and short laboratory experiments.
  * BTU students organise the advertising at the schools and the organisation of the participation in advance. The tasks of BTU students include the planning and execution of laboratory experiments in a team and the preparation of short handout papers. Each student gives a short lecture (15 min.) to a high-school audience. This presentation will be evaluated.

 |  
| Recommended Prerequisites:  | 
  * Basic knowledge in Biology, Cell Biology, Microbiology, Biotechnology and Biochemistry (from a respective study programme or other experience/background)
  * Interest in science promotion and public engagement with science and technology

 |  
| Mandatory Prerequisites:  | none  |  
| Forms of Teaching and Proportion:  | 
  * Tutorial / 4 Hours per Week per Semester 
  * Self organised studies / 120 Hours 

 |  
| Teaching Materials and Literature:  | will be provided  |  
| Module Examination:  | Continuous Assessment (MCA)  |  
| Assessment Mode for Module Examination:  | 
  * Organisation of the workshop including preparation and execution of laboratory experiments in microbiology, biochemistry and cell biology with high-school students: 40 %
  * Preparation of a handout for the own presentation; the handout must be handed in one week before the presentation event: 20%
  * Presentation:12 minutes: 40%

 |  
| Evaluation of Module Examination:  | Performance Verification – graded  |  
| Limited Number of Participants:  | None  |  
| Part of the Study Programme:  | 
  * no assignment

 |  
| This module has been approved for the general studies.  |  
| Remarks:  | No offer in WS 2025/26.  |  
| Module Components:  | 
  * Student Workshop School Meets Science (will be offered as a block course).
  * All meetings and Laboratory work take place at the Campus Senftenberg

 |  
| Components to be offered in the Current Semester:  | 
  * no assignment

 |
